reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Short title
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 2019 H.B. 126 history note, June 24, 2022 effective-date note, Revisor's Note (AG Opinion Letter No. 22-2022 and Governor Proclamation), and 2022 Dobbs annotation. Designates section 188.017 as the 'Right to Life of the Unborn Child Act' in archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Prohibition, medical emergency exception, penalties, and conspiracy bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and all source/Revisor/Dobbs notes. Archived text prohibits performing or inducing an abortion except in cases of medical emergency, classifies knowing violations as a class B felony with professional license suspension or revocation, and bars conspiracy prosecution of the woman upon whom the abortion is performed or induced; no claim of current enforceability.

headings.title: Medical emergency affirmative defense and burden of persuasion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and all source/Revisor/Dobbs notes. Establishes medical emergency as an affirmative defense to an alleged subsection 2 violation, placing the burden of persuasion (more probably true than not) on the defendant in the archived text.

headings.title: Contingent effective-date triggers and notification procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)-(3), footnote '*' (Effective 6-24-22), Revisor's Note citing AG Opinion Letter No. 22-2022 and Governor Proclamation of June 24, 2022, and Dobbs annotation. Sets out contingent effective-date notification triggers (Supreme Court overruling Roe v. Wade, federal constitutional amendment, or act of Congress); describes archived text and notes without asserting current enforceability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.017 (subsections 1-4 and subdivisions (4)(1)-(3)), 2019 H.B. 126 history note, June 24, 2022 effective-date footnote, Revisor's Note (AG Opinion Letter No. 22-2022 and Governor Proclamation), and 2022 Dobbs annotation; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked medical-emergency exception, affirmative defense burden, patient conspiracy prosecution bar, and contingent effective-date triggers. Retained all four neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: In-person initial drug administration and follow-up visit efforts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2013/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes. Requires the initial dose of RU-486 (mifepristone) or any abortion-inducing drug or chemical to be administered in the same room and physical presence of the prescribing or dispensing physician, and requires reasonable efforts for a follow-up visit unless termination is confirmed and assessed by a licensed physician before discharge; no claim of current enforceability.

headings.title: Department-approved complication plans and hospital emergency exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2013/2017 history notes. Requires DHSS approval of a physician's complication plan before prescribing or administering abortion-inducing drugs whose FDA label cites a clinical study with over one percent surgical intervention, except for medical-emergency inpatient hospital administration under hospital monitoring.

headings.title: Complication plan rulemaking, chapter 536, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017 effective-date note. Authorizes DHSS rules for complication plans subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 if applicable, with a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules adopted after October 24, 2017 if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.021 (subsections 1-3), 2013/2017 history notes, and October 24, 2017 effective-date note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked physical-presence administration, follow-up visit exception, FDA-label >1% surgical-intervention complication plan trigger and hospital medical-emergency inpatient exception, chapter 536/section 536.028 compliance, and post-October 24, 2017 nonseverability voidness clause. Retained all three neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Short title for sections 188.026 and 188.056 to 188.058
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2019 H.B. 126 history note. Designates sections 188.026, 188.056, 188.057, and 188.058 as the 'Missouri Stands for the Unborn Act'.

headings.title: Legislative findings on fetal development, legal precedent, and risks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including all subdivisions (1)-(36) and nested paragraphs (29)(a)-(b), (33)(a)-(d), and (35)(a)-(d), plus 2019 history note. Recites legislative findings on conception, Missouri statutory and case history, heartbeat/brain/pain development, D&E procedures, international and domestic comparisons, maternal short- and long-term risks, and gestational-age estimation error.

headings.title: Supremacy Clause and International Covenant ratification findings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2019 history note. Recites Article VI, Clause 2 of the U.S. Constitution and the U.S. ratification and non-self-executing declaration for the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights regarding shared state implementation responsibility.

headings.title: Stated implementation of International Covenant Article 6
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2019 history note. Quotes Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and states that Missouri implements it through state abortion regulation.

headings.title: Stated interests of the state of Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)-(8) and 2019 history note. Lists non-exhaustive stated state interests covering unborn life, childbirth, fetal pain, medical profession integrity, legal consistency across statutes, reducing later-pregnancy maternal risks, and avoiding health-system, taxpayer, and workforce burdens.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.026 (subsections 1-5, all 36 subdivisions of subsection 2 with nested paragraphs, and subdivisions (5)(1)-(8)) and 2019 H.B. 126 history note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked exact four-section short-title range (188.026, 188.056-188.058) and ensured neutral attribution ('Legislative findings', 'Stated implementation', 'Stated interests') without endorsing or asserting enforceability. Retained all five drafted titles.

headings.title: Seventy-two-hour informed consent disclosures, materials, and ultrasound
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including lead-in, subdivisions (1)-(8), nested paragraphs, 1979-2019 history notes, 2016 Whole Woman's Health v. Hellerstedt admitting-privileges annotation (relevant to (1)(e)), and 2019 Doe v. Parson RFRA annotation. Sets out non-emergency 72-hour informed consent requirements, in-person oral/written disclosures, department printed materials, ultrasound/heartbeat viewing opportunity, and right to withdraw consent; describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Private in-person presentation, reading assistance, and interpreters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and section annotations. Requires individual presentation of subsection 1 information in the woman's physical presence and a private room, plus reading materials aloud, providing an interpreter when needed, and answering questions in an understandable language.

headings.title: Patient written certification on department checklist form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section annotations. Prohibits performing or inducing an abortion until the woman certifies in writing on a department checklist form receipt of subsection 1 information, the ultrasound/heartbeat opportunity, and voluntary, informed, uncoerced consent.

headings.title: Uncoerced consent requirement and suspected-coercion assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 including subdivisions (1)-(3) and section annotations. Bars physicians from acting without voluntary, informed, uncoerced consent and requires providing private telephone access and information on section 455.003 rape crisis centers, section 455.200 domestic violence shelters, and chapter 455 orders of protection when coercion is suspected.

headings.title: Performing physician's seventy-two-hour in-person risk disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and section annotations. Requires the physician who will perform or induce the abortion personally to inform the woman orally and in person at least seventy-two hours beforehand of method-specific and anesthesia/medication/gestational-age/medical-history risks.

headings.title: Physician signature and medical-record retention of checklist
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and section annotations. Prohibits a physician from performing or inducing an abortion until receiving and signing a copy of the subsection 3 checklist form and requires retaining a copy in the patient's medical record.

headings.title: Written certification and retention for medical emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and section annotations. Requires a physician performing or inducing a medical-emergency abortion to certify the emergency's nature and circumstances in writing, sign the certification, and maintain it under section 188.060.

headings.title: Seventy-two-hour payment restriction and permitted payment notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and section annotations. Bars requiring, obtaining, or accepting abortion payment until seventy-two hours after subsection 1 information is provided, while expressly permitting notice that payment will be required after seventy-two hours if the patient voluntarily chooses to proceed. Reviewer revised title to clarify that payment notice is permitted rather than restricted; describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Definition of qualified professional and scope-of-practice limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and section annotations. Defines 'qualified professional' for section 188.027 as specified chapters 334, 335, or 337 licensees acting under the performing physician's supervision and within existing legal authority, without expanding licensure or scope of practice.

headings.title: Department printed materials, website, privacy, and hotline duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 text and section annotations. Directs DHSS by November 30, 2010 to produce legible, objective materials and forms at no cost, publish subsection 1 information on a monitored public website without collecting user identifying data, and operate a twenty-four-hour toll-free regional hotline.

headings.title: Emergency rulemaking under section 536.025
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 11 text and section annotations. Directs DHSS to use section 536.025 emergency rulemaking procedures to promulgate necessary rules, forms, and materials to implement section 188.027 by November 30, 2010.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour fallback if seventy-two-hour waiting period is enjoined
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 12 text and section annotations. Provides that if the seventy-two-hour waiting periods in subsections 1 and 8 are restrained or enjoined by judicial order, a twenty-four-hour waiting period applies, reverting to seventy-two hours if the order is stayed, dissolved, or ceases effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.027 (subsections 1-12 and all nested subdivisions/paragraphs), 1979-2019 history notes, 2016 Whole Woman's Health v. Hellerstedt admitting-privileges annotation, and 2019 Doe v. Parson RFRA annotation; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked medical-emergency exceptions, performing-physician vs. qualified-professional distinctions, November 30, 2010 material/emergency-rulemaking deadlines, and subsection 12 twenty-four-hour injunction fallback. Revised subsection 8 title to 'Seventy-two-hour payment restriction and permitted payment notice' to avoid implying payment notice is restricted; retained subsections 1-7 and 9-12 as neutral archived-text descriptions without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Minor consent, custodial-parent notice, and court-order alternatives
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)(a)-(f) and (2)-(4), 1979-2019 (effective 5-24-19) history notes, and four federal constitutional annotations (1981/1983 Ashcroft, 1985 C.L.G., 1986 T.L.J.). Bars non-emergency abortions on minors under eighteen absent minor plus one-parent/guardian consent and prior written notice to another joint-custody parent (with (a)-(f) exceptions), emancipation, or court self-consent or judicial consent. Reviewer broadened title to reflect emancipation and court-order alternatives in subdivisions (2)-(4); describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Juvenile court self-consent or judicial-consent procedures and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(5), paragraphs (3)(a)-(c), effective-date note, and federal annotations. Sets out juvenile court petition contents, five-day on-the-record hearing and appointed counsel, decree options, limited parental battery immunity and party costs, and expedited court of appeals review (twenty-four-hour notice and five-day perfection).

headings.title: Minor consent formalities and life-preservation exception to refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text, effective-date note, and federal annotations. Requires a minor desiring an abortion to be orally informed and, if possible, sign adult-manner written consent, and prohibits abortions against a minor's will except under a subsection 1(4) court order finding it necessary to preserve the minor's life.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.028 (subsections 1-3 and all subdivisions/paragraphs), 1979-2019 history notes, May 24, 2019 effective-date note, and four federal constitutional annotations (1981/1983 Ashcroft, 1985 C.L.G., 1986 T.L.J.); verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked medical-emergency exception, joint-custody parent notice exceptions (1)(a)-(f), juvenile court timelines/immunity/appeals, and subsection 3 refusal exception. Revised subsection 1 title to 'Minor consent, custodial-parent notice, and court-order alternatives' to reflect emancipation and judicial-consent options in (2)-(4); retained subsections 2-3 as neutral archived-text descriptions without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Post-viability prohibition, health exceptions, and major bodily function
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1974-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes, and 1983 Ashcroft annotation. Prohibits non-emergency abortions of viable unborn children unless necessary to preserve the woman's life or avert serious risk of substantial and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function, and provides a non-exhaustive definition of 'major bodily function'; no claim of current enforceability.

headings.title: Gestational-age, viability, reporting, method, and second-physician duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 including subdivisions (1)-(4), paragraphs (4)(a)-(e), history notes, and 1983 Ashcroft second-doctor annotation. Details non-emergency duties for gestational-age testing, viability testing at twenty-plus weeks, reporting/recordkeeping (citing section 188.052), independent second-physician concurrence (with section 197.020 same-hospital exception), life-preserving abortion method choice and certification, and a second attending physician for liveborn care.

headings.title: Criminal felony classification, imprisonment, and fine range
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section notes. Classifies knowing violations of section 188.030 as a class D felony carrying at least one year imprisonment and, notwithstanding section 558.002, a ten thousand to fifty thousand dollar fine in archived text.

headings.title: Physician license suspension or revocation under chapter 334
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and section notes. Subjects a physician convicted of or pleading guilty to violating section 188.030 to medical license suspension or revocation by the healing arts board under sections 334.100 and 334.103.

headings.title: Hospital license suspension or revocation under section 197.070
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and section notes. Provides that a licensed hospital knowingly allowing a violation of section 188.030 may face license suspension or revocation under section 197.070.

headings.title: Abortion facility license sanctions under section 197.220
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and section notes. Provides that a licensed abortion facility knowingly allowing a violation of section 188.030 may face license suspension or revocation under section 197.220.

headings.title: Bar on conspiracy prosecution of the patient
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and section notes. Prohibits prosecuting a woman upon whom an abortion is performed or induced in violation of section 188.030 for conspiracy to violate the section.

headings.title: Construction against creating an abortion right
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and section notes. States that section 188.030 neither creates nor recognizes a right to abortion nor makes lawful any currently unlawful abortion.

headings.title: Severability under section 1.140
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and section notes. Expresses legislative intent that section 188.030 be severable as noted in section 1.140 if any part is declared invalid under federal or state constitutions.

headings.title: Legislative sponsor intervention in constitutional challenges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 text and section notes. Authorizes the general assembly by concurrent resolution to appoint one or more official sponsoring or co-sponsoring members to intervene as a matter of right in constitutional challenges to the law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.030 (subsections 1-10 and all subdivisions/paragraphs in subsection 2), 1974-2017 history notes, October 24, 2017 effective-date note, and 1983 Ashcroft second-doctor annotation; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked medical-emergency exceptions, viability/reporting/second-physician duties (citing sections 188.052 and 197.020), class D felony/fine/licensing cross-references (sections 558.002, 334.100, 334.103, 197.070, 197.220), patient conspiracy bar, section 1.140 severability, and concurrent-resolution intervention. Retained all ten neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Short title
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1974-2026 (S.B. 999) history note, and nonseverability note referencing section 1.1008. Designates section 188.035 as the 'Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act'.

headings.title: Legal rights and status of child born alive
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Declares that a child born alive during or after an abortion or attempted abortion has all rights, privileges, and immunities of other persons, citizens, and residents, including other liveborn children.

headings.title: Provider standard of care for liveborn child
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Requires licensed, registered, or certified health care providers present in a professional capacity when a child is born alive during or after an abortion or attempted abortion to exercise the same professional skill, care, and diligence as for any other liveborn child at the same gestational age.

headings.title: First degree murder liability for killing liveborn child
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Provides that knowingly performing or attempting an overt act that kills a child born alive described in subsection 3 constitutes first degree murder under section 565.020.

headings.title: Civil cause of action and nonexclusive remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Recognizes a civil cause of action under sections 537.080 to 537.090 or chapter 538 for injury from a subsection 3 violation, nonexclusive of administrative or criminal actions.

headings.title: Definition of born alive under federal statute
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Incorporates the definition of 'born alive' from 1 U.S.C. Section 8(b) for section 188.035.

headings.title: Exclusion of previability natural spontaneous loss
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text, 2026 S.B. 999 history note, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note. Clarifies that natural and spontaneous loss of an unborn child before fetal viability is not construed as an abortion under section 188.015.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.035 (subsections 1-7), 1974-2026 (S.B. 999) history notes, and section 1.1008 nonseverability note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked liveborn child status, licensed/registered/certified provider care duty, first-degree murder provision for overt act or attempt under section 565.020, sections 537.080-537.090/chapter 538 nonexclusive civil action, 1 U.S.C. Section 8(b) cross-reference, and section 188.015 previability spontaneous-loss exclusion. Retained all seven neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Prohibition on performing abortions for tissue transplantation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1988 H.B. 1479 history note. Prohibits a physician from performing an abortion knowing the woman conceived the unborn child and intends to procure the abortion to provide fetal organs or tissue for medical transplantation.

headings.title: Prohibition on transplanting tissue from procured abortions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1988 history note. Prohibits utilizing fetal organs or tissue from an abortion for medical transplantation knowing the abortion was procured for that use.

headings.title: Ban on inducements to conceive for tissue use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1988 history note. Prohibits offering monetary or other inducements to a woman or prospective father to conceive an unborn child for medical, scientific, experimental, or therapeutic use of fetal organs or tissue.

headings.title: Ban on inducements to abort for tissue use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 1988 history note. Prohibits offering monetary or other inducements to the mother or father of an unborn child to procure an abortion for medical, scientific, experimental, or therapeutic use of fetal organs or tissue.

headings.title: Valuable consideration ban with burial and examination exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 1988 history note. Prohibits knowingly offering or receiving valuable consideration for fetal organs or tissue from an abortion, while expressly excepting payment for burial or final disposition or for pathological, autopsy, or postmortem examination.

headings.title: Severability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 1988 history note. Declares all provisions and applications of section 188.036 severable if any provision or application is held invalid.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.036 (subsections 1-6) and 1988 H.B. 1479 history note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked knowledge elements for transplantation bans, inducement bans for conception vs. abortion, valuable consideration exceptions (burial/final disposition and pathological/autopsy/postmortem examination), and severability clause. Retained all six neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Legislative findings on discrimination and selective abortions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(6), 2019 H.B. 126 history note, and original-rolls footnote ('Words "a half" appear in original rolls' in subdivision (4)). Sets out general assembly findings on bias and discrimination against pregnant women and unborn children, historical coercive family planning, Missouri demographic statistics, sex selection, and Down Syndrome.

headings.title: Prohibition on abortions solely for Down Syndrome indication
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2019 history note. Prohibits performing or inducing an abortion knowing the woman seeks it solely because of a prenatal diagnosis, test, or screening indicating Down Syndrome or potential Down Syndrome; describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Prohibition on abortions solely for sex or race
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2019 history note. Prohibits performing or inducing an abortion knowing the woman seeks it solely because of the unborn child's sex or race; describes archived text without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Applicable civil penalties including sections 188.065 and 188.085
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2019 history note. Subjects any physician or other person performing, inducing, or attempting an abortion prohibited by section 188.038 to applicable civil penalties under chapter 188, expressly citing sections 188.065 and 188.085.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.038 (subsections 1-4 and subdivisions (1)(1)-(6)), 2019 H.B. 126 history note, and original-rolls footnote ('Words "a half" appear in original rolls' in (1)(4)); verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked knowledge and sole-purpose qualifiers in subsections 2-3 and civil-penalty cross-references to sections 188.065 and 188.085 (including attempts). Retained all four neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Definition of medical emergency for section 188.039
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1979-2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes, and 1987 Webster (permanent injunction of earlier version) and 2006 Nixon (state constitutional ruling on 24-hour waiting period) annotations. Defines 'medical emergency' specifically for section 188.039 based on good faith clinical judgment; no claim of current enforceability.

headings.title: Seventy-two-hour risk conference and prescription timing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, effective-date note, and Webster/Nixon annotations. Requires a non-emergency conference at least seventy-two hours before an abortion (or before writing/communicating the first drug prescription) with the performing physician, qualified professional, or referring physician on indicators, contraindicators, and risk factors, with only one conference required per abortion.

headings.title: Patient risk-factor evaluation during conference
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section annotations. Requires evaluating the patient during the conference for physical, psychological, or situational indicators, contraindicators, and risk factors that predispose to or increase short- or long-term adverse health reactions.

headings.title: Signed consent statement and confidential file retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and section annotations. Requires both provider and patient (if choosing to proceed) to sign a written informed-consent statement at the end of the conference and maintain executed statements in the patient's medical file subject to state confidentiality laws and rules.

headings.title: Department model consent form and non-excusal of duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and section annotations. Directs the DHSS director to disseminate an optional model written statement form while specifying that unavailability of the model form does not affect subsections 2 to 4 duties.

headings.title: Definition of qualified professional and scope-of-practice limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and section annotations. Defines 'qualified professional' for section 188.039 as specified chapters 334, 335, or 337 licensees under the performing physician's supervision within existing authority, without expanding licensure or scope of practice.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour fallback if seventy-two-hour waiting period is enjoined
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and section annotations. Replaces subsection 2's seventy-two-hour waiting period with a twenty-four-hour waiting period if restrained or enjoined by judicial order, restoring seventy-two hours if the order is stayed, dissolved, or ceases effect.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.039 (subsections 1-7), 1979-2017 history notes, October 24, 2017 effective-date note, 1987 Webster permanent-injunction annotation (prior version), and 2006 Nixon state-constitutional annotation; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked section-specific medical-emergency and qualified-professional definitions, 72-hour conference/prescription timing and one-conference limit, optional model form non-excusal rule, and subsection 7 twenty-four-hour injunction fallback. Retained all seven neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Minimum medical malpractice insurance coverage requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2003/2019 history note. Prohibits performing or inducing an abortion without medical malpractice insurance of at least one million dollars per occurrence and three million dollars annual aggregate.

headings.title: Definition of medical malpractice insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2003/2019 history note. Defines 'medical malpractice insurance' specifically for section 188.043 as coverage against legal liability and claim-incident loss, damage, or expense from death or injury caused by health care provider negligence or malpractice.

headings.title: Facility and hospital hiring ban and employer-provided coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2003/2019 history note. Prohibits abortion facilities and hospitals from employing or engaging uninsured persons to perform or induce abortions, unless the facility or hospital provides coverage meeting section 188.043 minimums.

headings.title: Licensing sanctions for failing to maintain coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2003/2019 history note. Operates notwithstanding section 334.100 to make failure to maintain required medical malpractice insurance an additional ground for sanctioning a license, certificate, or permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.043 (subsections 1-4) and 2003/2019 history note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked $1M/$3M coverage thresholds, section-specific definition, abortion facility and hospital hiring ban with employer-coverage exception, and section 334.100 licensing-sanction override. Retained all four neutral archived-text titles without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Twenty-one-year tail insurance requirement for specified drugs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2019 H.B. 126 history note. Requires at least one million/three million dollar tail insurance maintained for twenty-one years (in addition to section 188.043) for injury or death of a surviving child when an abortion-inducing drug or chemical carries a manufacturer, peer-reviewed journal, or FDA label warning of birth defects, disability, or other injury.

headings.title: Definition of tail insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2019 history note. Defines 'tail insurance' for section 188.044 as coverage for insured legal liability on post-cancellation, nonrenewal, or post-termination claims arising from acts during the prior medical malpractice policy period.

headings.title: Facility and hospital hiring ban and employer-provided tail coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2019 history note. Prohibits abortion facilities and hospitals from employing or engaging persons lacking required tail insurance to induce abortions using covered drugs, unless the facility or hospital provides compliant coverage amounts and duration. Reviewer added 'and hospital' to reflect full party scope matching section 188.043(3).

headings.title: Licensing sanctions for failing to maintain tail coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2019 history note. Operates notwithstanding section 334.100 to make failure to maintain required tail insurance an additional ground for sanctioning a license, certificate, or permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.044 (subsections 1-4) and 2019 H.B. 126 history note; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked warning-triggered 21-year $1M/$3M tail-insurance requirement supplementing section 188.043, tail-insurance definition, and section 334.100 licensing-sanction override. Revised subsection 3 title to 'Facility and hospital hiring ban and employer-provided tail coverage' to include hospitals alongside abortion facilities; retained subsections 1-2 and 4 without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Pathologist tissue submission, report deadlines, and non-completion notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text, 1979/2017 (effective 10-24-17) history notes, and 1983 Ashcroft pathology-report annotation. Requires five-day submission of removed abortion tissue (except subsection 5 tissue) to a board-eligible or certified pathologist, DHSS filing, seventy-two-hour facility/hospital copy for the permanent record, and twenty-four-hour notice if examination fails to identify evidence of a completed abortion.

headings.title: Department report reconciliation, inquiries, and unscheduled inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text, effective-date note, and Ashcroft annotation. Requires DHSS to reconcile abortion notices with tissue reports, inquire into missing reports, and treat unsatisfactory noncompliance as a deficiency requiring an unscheduled inspection subject to chapter 197 license suspension, review, and appeal procedures.

headings.title: Annual department report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and section notes. Requires an annual DHSS report to the general assembly beginning January 1, 2018 detailing facility deficiencies, inquiries, remediation, aggregated de-identified procedure/complication/tissue-report counts, and section 188.052 inconsistencies, while barring legally prohibited personal patient disclosures.

headings.title: Confidentiality of patient, staff, and physician information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and section notes. Requires all DHSS reports to the general assembly under section 188.047 to maintain confidentiality of personal information of patients, facility personnel, and facility physicians.

headings.title: Permitted medical, scientific, paternity, and law enforcement tissue uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and section notes. Clarifies that section 188.047 does not prohibit using fetal organs or tissue from an abortion for medical or scientific determinations of anomaly, illness, death, genetic condition, or paternity, or for law enforcement purposes.

headings.title: Reporting rulemaking authority, chapter 536, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 2017 effective-date note. Authorizes DHSS rules governing section 188.047 reports subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 if applicable, with a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules adopted after October 24, 2017 if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived section 188.047 (subsections 1-6), 1979/2017 history notes, October 24, 2017 effective-date note, and 1983 Ashcroft pathology-report annotation; verified sourceUrl and all SHA-256 fingerprints. headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1974-2017 history notes. Establishes a medical-emergency affirmative defense for any alleged violation of chapter 188 across criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings, placing the burden of persuasion on the defendant.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017 effective-date note. Prohibits employer discrimination, adverse classification, or retaliation based on refusal to participate in abortion or protected opposition/proceedings under sections 188.100 to 188.120, and bars any person from aiding, abetting, inciting, compelling, or coercing forbidden acts.

headings.title: Undue hardship and bona fide occupational qualification exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1986 history note. Operates notwithstanding sections 188.100 to 188.120 to except subsection 1 acts when reasonable accommodation creates undue hardship on the business or enterprise or participation in abortion is a bona fide occupational qualification.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 1986 history note. Clarifies that sections 188.100 to 188.120 do not require employers to grant preferential treatment because of an individual's refusal to participate in abortion.

headings.title: Nondiscrimination by colleges, universities, and hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 1986 H.B. 1596 history note. Prohibits public or private colleges, universities, and hospitals from discriminating against any person for refusing to participate in abortion.

headings.title: Conscience exemption from school fees funding abortions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 1986 history note. Exempts school applicants, students, teachers, and employees giving written conscience or belief notice from paying fees funding abortions for others, while allowing collection of non-abortion fee portions if reasonably segregated.

headings.title: Legislative intent regarding agency speech and conscience rights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2017 (effective 10-24-17) history note. States legislative intent acknowledging alternatives-to-abortion agencies' operational and speech rights and persons' right against government-compelled participation in abortion contrary to religious beliefs or moral convictions.

headings.title: Preemption of local restrictions on alternatives-to-abortion agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2017 history note. Preempts political subdivision orders, ordinances, rules, regulations, or policies prohibiting, restricting, interfering with, or adversely affecting operations or speech of alternatives-to-abortion agencies or their personnel.

headings.title: Preserved local zoning, land-use, building, and fire codes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2017 history note. Preserves political subdivision zoning, land-use, building, and fire code authority if alternatives-to-abortion agencies are treated like similarly situated agencies without circumventing subsection 2.

headings.title: Preemption of local mandates to participate in abortion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and 2017 history note. Preempts political subdivision measures having the purpose or effect of requiring direct or indirect participation in abortion contrary to religious beliefs or moral convictions.

headings.title: Preemption of local real estate mandates involving abortion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 text and 2017 history note. Preempts political subdivision measures requiring chapter 339 real estate licensees, appraisers, property owners, or others to conduct real estate transactions involving abortion facilities or non-lifesaving abortions contrary to religious beliefs or moral convictions.

headings.title: Preemption of local health-plan benefit mandates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 text and 2017 history note. Preempts political subdivision measures requiring employers, employees, health plan providers or sponsors, health care providers, or others to provide coverage for or participate in health plan benefits not otherwise required by state law.

headings.title: Authorized equitable relief, damages, fees, and nonexclusive remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 text and 2017 history note. Authorizes courts in enforcement actions to order injunctive or equitable relief, damages or legal remedies, and reasonable attorney's fees, costs, and expenses, nonexclusive of other legal remedies.

headings.title: Private and attorney general enforcement standing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 text and 2017 history note. Authorizes the attorney general to bring enforcement actions in addition to private causes of action by persons whose section 188.125 rights are violated.

headings.title: Permitted local assistance and funding for pregnancy support
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 text and 2017 history note. Clarifies that section 188.125 does not prohibit political subdivisions from enacting measures to assist pregnant women in carrying to term, caring for children, or adoption, including funding alternatives-to-abortion agencies.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 text and section notes. Provides that an unemancipated minor lacks capacity to consent to any action violating section 188.250 or section 188.028.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and section notes. headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 text and 2019 H.B. 126 history note. Designates section 188.375 as the 'Late-Term Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act'.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 text and 2019 history note. Defines 'late-term pain-capable unborn child' for section 188.375 as an unborn child at twenty weeks gestational age or later.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 text and 2019 history note.
